name: Seated Machine Hip Adduction
variant: Seated hip-adduction machine with medial thigh pads and guided resistance toward the body midline.
description: Sit with the pelvis and trunk fixed against the pads, place the inside of the thighs against the pads, brace lightly, squeeze the thighs inward through a controlled hip-adduction range, pause without rocking the trunk, then return under control until the stack is close to resting.

hypertrophy.rationale: Useful direct inner-thigh stimulus, but visible scoring is conservative because the current map represents adductor longus rather than the whole adductor group.

strength.rationale: Builds isolated hip-adduction force, but does not express integrated lower-body strength.

joint_resilience.rationale: Can load hip-adductor capacity in a controlled range and may be useful as a groin-capacity accessory, but the seated guided task is not the same as sport-speed adduction or cutting demands.

athletic_transfer.rationale: Has narrow transfer through adductor capacity, but low direct transfer because the task is seated, supported, and single-joint.

control.rationale: Very low Motor Control demand beyond posture, range, and avoiding trunk or pelvic compensation.

fatigue_efficiency.rationale: Good local adductor stimulus with low systemic fatigue and low unrelated recovery cost.

setup.rationale: Requires the machine and pad setting, but loading is quick and repeatable once seated.

ease.rationale: Simple guided movement with very low balance and coordination demand.

progression.rationale: Load, reps, range, and tempo are easy to track, with deductions for stack increments and machine-specific geometry.

support.rationale: Very high external support from the seat, back pad, handles, thigh pads, and guided lever path.

primary.name: Adductor longus
primary.evidenceShort: Machine hip adduction and adductor-exercise EMG support adductor longus as a primary visible target.
primary.evidence: Machine hip-adduction EMG and broader hip-adduction exercise evidence support the adductor group as the target. The app currently shows adductor longus because it is the local adductor mesh available.

evidence.verdict: Seated machine hip adduction: adductor longus primary; no visible secondary or support muscles added.
evidence.clinicalShort: EMG estimates acute excitation; it should not be treated as a direct measure of hypertrophy, injury prevention, pain response, or individual adaptation.
evidence.limitsShort: Hip flexion angle, starting width, pad height, pelvis motion, range, load, and machine geometry can shift adductor longus, adductor magnus, gracilis, and pectineus contribution.
evidence.summary: The seated machine hip adduction is classified as a guided lower-body hip-adduction isolation exercise. Machine EMG and adductor exercise evidence support a primary adductor target role, but the visible MVP map is intentionally limited to adductor longus because broader adductor meshes are not yet in the local anatomy registry.
evidence.clinicalInterpretation: The machine is useful for controlled inner-thigh loading, but it should not be equated with Copenhagen adduction, cutting, skating, sprinting, or other high-control groin tasks. Those movements should have separate entries if added.
evidence.limitations: The visible map underrepresents the full adductor complex because adductor magnus, adductor brevis, gracilis, and pectineus are not currently exposed as local meshes.

studies.type: Machine versus elastic hip abduction/adduction EMG
studies.finding: Hip adduction and abduction exercises using isotonic machines and elastic resistance produced load-related EMG responses in the target hip muscles.
studies.citation: Brandt M, Jakobsen MD, Thorborg K, Sundstrup EH, Jay K, Andersen LL. Perceived loading and muscle activity during hip strengthening exercises: comparison of elastic resistance and machine exercises. International Journal of Sports Physical Therapy. 2013;8(6):811-819.
studies.relevance: Close machine-specific EMG source for hip adduction loading, repeatability, and machine limitations.

studies.shortCitation: Serner et al., Br J Sports Med, 2014
studies.finding: Adductor longus activity differed substantially across common hip-adduction exercises used for groin injury prevention and rehabilitation.
studies.citation: Serner A, Jakobsen MD, Andersen LL, Holmich P, Sundstrup E, Thorborg K. EMG evaluation of hip adduction exercises for soccer players: implications for exercise selection in prevention and treatment of groin injuries. British Journal of Sports Medicine. 2014;48(14):1108-1114. doi:10.1136/bjsports-2012-091746.
studies.relevance: Adductor longus EMG source for hip-adduction role boundaries and groin-capacity interpretation.

studies.shortCitation: Ishoi et al., Scand J Med Sci Sports, 2016
studies.finding: An eight-week Copenhagen adduction intervention increased eccentric hip-adduction strength in soccer players.
studies.citation: Ishoi L, Sorensen CN, Kaae NM, Jorgensen LB, Holmich P, Serner A. Large eccentric strength increase using the Copenhagen Adduction exercise in football: A randomized controlled trial. Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports. 2016;26(11):1334-1342. doi:10.1111/sms.12585.
studies.relevance: Movement-family source for adductor strength adaptation; used to contextualize machine adduction as a lower-control accessory rather than a sport-transfer equivalent.
